docs.title: StarEau plugin
docs.text:
The StarEau plugin helps to manage the data of underground water networks (drinking water, wastewater and stormwater) with QGIS and PostGIS, in accordance with the French StaR'Eau geostandard.

docs.title: Presentation of the plugin concepts
docs.text:
The StarEau plugin helps to manage the data of underground water networks with QGIS and PostGIS:

  • drinking water networks (AEP, alimentation en eau potable),
  • sanitation networks (ASS, assainissement): wastewater, stormwater and combined sewers.

The data model is the StaR'Eau geostandard, published by the CNIG (Conseil national de l'information géolocalisée) and the ASTEE. The SQL files of the geostandard are available in the StaR-Eau repository: the plugin installs them and adds its own functions and triggers to keep the network topology consistent and to analyse the network.

docs.title: Network types
docs.text:
Each object of the network has a network type, stored in the field type_reseau (value list com_type_reseau):

Code Network aep Drinking water assaeu Wastewater assaep Stormwater assaru Combined sewer (réseau unitaire) ince Fire fighting

The plugin tools work either on the AEP network (type_reseau = 'aep') or on the ASS network (all the other network types). A pipe is never linked to a node of the other network family.

docs.title: Nodes and pipes
docs.text:
The network is a graph made of network nodes and pipes:

  • a network node (nœud réseau) is a point: a valve, a manhole, a reservoir, a pumping station, etc.,
  • a pipe (canalisation) is a line linking two nodes:
    • its initial node (noeudinitial), at the start point of the line,
    • its terminal node (noeudterminal), at the end point of the line.

The direction of the line is meaningful: from the initial node to the terminal node. For a sanitation network, it is the flow direction, used to walk the network upstream and downstream.

When there is no node at the start or end point of a pipe, the field noeudinitial or noeudterminal contains the value non_renseigne: it is a missing node, which can be found with the algorithm Get missing nodes.

The links between pipes and nodes are maintained automatically by the database, see Network topology.

docs.title: Table inheritance
docs.text:
The StaR'Eau data model uses the PostgreSQL table inheritance:

  • the table stareau_principale.noeud_reseau is the parent of all the node tables: aep_vanne, aep_reservoir, ass_regard, ass_pompage, etc.,
  • the table stareau_principale.canalisation is the parent of all the pipe tables: aep_canalisation, ass_canalisation, aep_canalisation_branchement, etc.,
  • all these tables also inherit the common fields of stareau_principale.champ_commun: network type, service status, INSEE code of the municipality, owner, operator, XY and Z precisions, dates, etc.

The data is stored in the child tables, e.g. a valve in stareau_aep.aep_vanne. A query on a parent table returns the objects of all its child tables: stareau_principale.noeud_reseau contains all the nodes of all the networks. The identifiers fid, id_noeud_reseau and id_canalisation are therefore unique across all the child tables.

docs.title: Value lists
docs.text:
Most fields contain a code from a value list, stored in the schema stareau_valeur (one table per list, with the fields code, valeur and description). For example, the field etat_ouverture of a valve uses the list aep_etat_ouverture: ouverte, fermee, partiel_ouverte, partiel_fermee.

Besides the values of the geostandard, every list contains the values non_renseigne, non_concerne, non_valide, non_determine and autre.

docs.title: Network analysis
docs.text:
Some tools use the extension pgRouting to find paths in the drinking water network:

  • the pipes between a node and the nearest target: water intake, treatment plant, reservoir,
  • the pipes between the water intakes and the treatment plants, or between the treatment plants and the reservoirs, to check the function of the pipes,
  • the valves to close to isolate a part of the network.

These tools use a routing graph computed from the AEP nodes and pipes, see Network analysis.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Concept French Definition AEP Alimentation en eau potable Drinking water network ASS Assainissement Sanitation network: wastewater, stormwater, combined sewer Network node Nœud réseau Point object of the network linked to the pipes: valve, manhole, reservoir, etc. Pipe Canalisation Line between an initial node and a terminal node Service connection Branchement Part of the network between the main pipe and the user (schemas *_brcht) Missing node Nœud manquant Start or end point of a pipe without any network node Orphan node Nœud orphelin Network node which is not the initial or terminal node of any pipe Duplicate node Nœud en doublon Orphan node located at the same place as another node Water intake Captage Point where the raw water is taken from the resource Treatment plant Traitement Drinking water treatment plant Reservoir Réservoir Water tank or water tower Valve Vanne Device used to open or close a pipe Manhole Regard Access point to a sanitation pipe PEI Point d'eau incendie Fire hydrant or fire water point (schema stareau_defense_incendie) Vertex / Edge Node / pipe of the pgRouting graph, see Network analysis

docs.title: Useful functions
docs.text:
The stareau schema provides SQL functions which can be used directly in your queries, for example in the QGIS Browser panel (right-click on the PostgreSQL connection or schema, then Execute SQL…), in the QGIS DB Manager, in psql or in a virtual layer built on a PostgreSQL query.

The examples below use the default schema name stareau and the coordinate reference system EPSG:2154.

docs.title: Network check functions
docs.text:
Function Usage stareau.aep_noeud_manquant(), stareau.ass_noeud_manquant() Missing nodes of the AEP or ASS network stareau.aep_noeud_orphelin(), stareau.ass_noeud_orphelin() Orphan nodes of the AEP or ASS network stareau.aep_noeud_doublon(), stareau.ass_noeud_doublon() Duplicate nodes of the AEP or ASS network

These functions are used by the network check algorithms.

docs.title: Missing nodes
docs.text:
stareau.ass_noeud_manquant() and stareau.aep_noeud_manquant() return the start and end points of the pipes whose initial or terminal node is non_renseigne, with the fields fid, geom, id_canalisation_upstream and id_canalisation_downstream.

-- Number of missing nodes of the sanitation network
SELECT count(*) FROM stareau.ass_noeud_manquant();

docs.title: Orphan nodes
docs.text:
stareau.ass_noeud_orphelin() and stareau.aep_noeud_orphelin() return the network nodes (all the fields of stareau_principale.noeud_reseau) which are not the initial or terminal node of any pipe.

-- Orphan nodes of the drinking water network, with the name of their table
SELECT n.tableoid::regclass AS table_name, n.fid, n.id_noeud_reseau
FROM stareau.aep_noeud_orphelin() AS n;

docs.title: Duplicate nodes
docs.text: stareau.ass_noeud_doublon() and stareau.aep_noeud_doublon() return the orphan nodes located at the same place as another network node.

docs.title: Sanitation network functions
docs.text:
Function Usage stareau.ass_downstream(id_noeud_reseau) Pipes downstream of a node stareau.ass_upstream(id_noeud_reseau) Pipes upstream of a node

These functions walk the sanitation network recursively, following the direction of the pipes, from the node with the given id_noeud_reseau. They do not need pgRouting. They are used by the actions Downstream and Upstream.

They return one line per pipe, with the fields:

Field Description idx Step of the walk, from 1 for the pipes connected to the node fid_canalisation fid of the pipe fid_noeudinitial, id_noeudinitial fid and id_noeud_reseau of the initial node of the pipe fid_noeudterminal, id_noeudterminal fid and id_noeud_reseau of the terminal node of the pipe

Example: total length of the pipes downstream of a manhole:

SELECT sum(ST_Length(c.geom)) AS length
FROM stareau.ass_downstream('ac05c1e8-2c1f-4a8e-9bf7-3a2a7bd7dc0b') AS d
JOIN stareau_principale.canalisation AS c ON c.fid = d.fid_canalisation;

docs.title: Network analysis functions (pgRouting)
docs.text:
Function Usage aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target Pipes between a node and the nearest target aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target_avoiding_closed_valves Same, without crossing the closed valves aep_pgr_find_captages_from_traitement Adduction pipes between a treatment plant and its water intakes aep_pgr_nearest_vannes Valves to close to isolate a point or a node aep_pgr_nearest_closed_vannes Closed valves isolating a point

These functions need the pgRouting extension and an up to date routing graph (tables stareau.aep_vertex and stareau.aep_edge): run the algorithm Fill AEP vertices and edges beforehand. See Network analysis.

The identifier of a vertex of the graph is the fid of the network node.

docs.title: Path to the nearest target
docs.text:
stareau.aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target(vertex_id, target_schema, target_table) returns the pipes (all the fields of stareau_aep.aep_canalisation) of the shortest path between a node and the nearest object of the target table:

  • vertex_id: the fid of the start node,
  • target_schema: the schema of the target table, e.g. stareau_aep,
  • target_table: the target table, e.g. aep_captage, aep_traitement or aep_reservoir.

Only the 10 targets closest to the node (as the crow flies) are tested.

-- Pipes between the water intake 12 and the nearest treatment plant
SELECT fid, fonction_canalisation, ST_Length(geom) AS length
FROM stareau.aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target(12, 'stareau_aep', 'aep_traitement');

stareau.aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target_avoiding_closed_valves(vertex_id, target_schema, target_table) has the same parameters, but the pipes connected to a closed valve (etat_ouverture = 'fermee') are not used.

docs.title: Water intakes of a treatment plant
docs.text:
stareau.aep_pgr_find_captages_from_traitement(vertex_id, target_schema, target_table) returns the pipes of the paths between a treatment plant and the water intakes which supply it, using only the adduction pipes (fonction_canalisation = 'adduction'):

SELECT DISTINCT fid
FROM stareau.aep_pgr_find_captages_from_traitement(25, 'stareau_aep', 'aep_captage');

Unlike aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target, the paths to all the reachable water intakes are returned (among the 10 closest ones).

docs.title: Nearest valves
docs.text:
stareau.aep_pgr_nearest_vannes(the_point) returns the valves (all the fields of stareau_aep.aep_vanne) to close to isolate a point of the drinking water network:

  • the_point: a point geometry, located less than 5 m from a pipe of the graph.

The walk starts from the pipe closest to the point, in both directions, and stops at the first valve met on each branch. Only the 100 valves closest to the point are tested.

SELECT fid, id_noeud_reseau, etat_ouverture
FROM stareau.aep_pgr_nearest_vannes(
    ST_GeomFromText('POINT(785691.35 6272226.25)', 2154)
);

stareau.aep_pgr_nearest_closed_vannes(the_point) does the same with the closed valves only: the open valves are crossed.

stareau.aep_pgr_nearest_vannes(vertex_id) is a variant starting from a network node, given by its fid.

docs.title: Trigger functions
docs.text:
Function Usage stareau.aa_before_geometry_insert_or_update_reduce_precision() Round the coordinates to 5 cm stareau.before_canalisation_insert_or_update() Link a pipe to its initial and terminal nodes stareau.after_noeud_reseau_insert_or_update() Link the pipes to a new node, move the pipes with a node stareau.after_noeud_reseau_delete() Unlink the pipes of a deleted node

See Network topology for the rules applied by these functions.

docs.title: Other functions
docs.text: stareau.get_current_setting(setting_name, default_value, value_type) returns the value of a PostgreSQL setting, or the default value if the setting is not set or invalid. It is used by the trigger functions to read the setting stareau.graph.disable.trigger.

docs.title: Database structure
docs.text:
The documentation of all the schemas of the plugin (tables, views, columns, constraints, relationships and functions) is generated by SchemaSpy. Select a schema to see its tables and relationships: most of the relationships are foreign keys from the network tables to the value lists of the schema stareau_valeur. The tables of the StaR'Eau geostandard are described in Tables and fields.

Open the database documentation in a new tab

docs.title: Tables and fields
docs.text:
The plugin installs the tables of the StaR'Eau geostandard, split in several schemas, and its own schema stareau. The names below use the default schema name stareau: all the schemas are prefixed by the schema name chosen when creating the database structure.

For the complete description of the StaR'Eau tables and fields, see the documentation of the geostandard in the StaR-Eau repository. The tables and fields of the database also have comments, visible in the QGIS Browser panel or with SchemaSpy.

For the technical details of the schemas (types, constraints, relationships, indexes, functions, etc.), see the Database structure.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Schema Content stareau Functions and triggers of the plugin, routing graph, metadata stareau_principale Parent tables: champ_commun, noeud_reseau, canalisation, dimension, emprise stareau_commun Tables shared by the AEP and ASS networks: pluviometre, piezometre, point_geolocalisation stareau_aep Drinking water network: aep_canalisation, aep_captage, aep_traitement, aep_reservoir, aep_vanne, aep_pompage, aep_regulation, aep_appareillage, aep_point_mesure, aep_piece, etc. stareau_aep_brcht Drinking water service connections: aep_canalisation_branchement, aep_point_livraison, aep_raccord, aep_vanne_branchement, aep_piece_branchement stareau_ass Sanitation network: ass_canalisation, ass_regard, ass_pompage, ass_traitement, ass_bassin, ass_exutoire, ass_equipement, ass_ouvrage_special_*, ass_gestion_epl_*, etc. stareau_ass_brcht Sanitation service connections: ass_canalisation_branchement, ass_point_collecte, ass_raccord, ass_engouffrement_* stareau_defense_incendie Fire water points: pei and its value lists stareau_valeur Value lists

The tables *_affleurant, *_genie_civil, *_perimetre_gestion and *_protection_mecanique are created in both schemas stareau_aep and stareau_ass.

docs.title: Main tables
docs.text: The tables of the network objects inherit from the parent tables of the schema stareau_principale (see Table inheritance): they have all the fields described below, and their own specific fields.

docs.title: champ_commun
docs.text:
The common fields of all the network objects. This table contains no data.

Field Type Description type_reseau text Network type: aep, assaeu, assaep, assaru, ince (list com_type_reseau) fictif boolean If the object is fictitious, e.g. a node added to link two pipes. Default: False. etat_service text Service status (list com_etat_service) insee_commune text INSEE code of the municipality localisation text Address, name of the main street, or relative location of the object maitre_ouvrage text Owner exploitant text Current operator entreprise_pose text Company which installed the object precision_xy, precision_z text Precision class of the XY and Z coordinates (list com_precision) an_pose_inf, an_pose_sup integer Start and end years of the installation period. an_pose_sup is -9999 if unknown. an_service_inf, an_service_sup integer Start and end years of the commissioning period an_abandon_inf, an_abandon_sup integer Start and end years of the decommissioning period an_rehab_inf, an_rehab_sup integer Start and end years of the rehabilitation period date_creation, origine_creation timestamp, text Date and origin of the creation of the object date_maj, origine_maj timestamp, text Date and origin of the last update of the object lien_doc1, lien_doc2 text Links to documents commentaire text Comment

docs.title: noeud_reseau
docs.text:
The network nodes: parent table of all the point objects of the networks (aep_vanne, aep_reservoir, ass_regard, etc.).

Field Type Description fid integer Unique identifier (automatic), unique across all the node tables id_noeud_reseau text Identifier of the node used by the pipes. Unique. A UUID by default. geom Point Geometry of the node. Its coordinates are rounded to 5 cm.

docs.title: canalisation
docs.text:
The pipes: parent table of all the pipe tables (aep_canalisation, ass_canalisation, aep_canalisation_branchement, ass_canalisation_branchement).

Field Type Description fid integer Unique identifier (automatic), unique across all the pipe tables id_canalisation text Identifier of the pipe. Unique. A UUID by default. geom LineString Geometry of the pipe, from the initial node to the terminal node noeudinitial text id_noeud_reseau of the initial node, or non_renseigne. Filled automatically. noeudterminal text id_noeud_reseau of the terminal node, or non_renseigne. Filled automatically. mode_circulation text Flow mode (list com_mode_circulation) type_pose text Laying type (list com_type_pose) raison_pose text Reason for laying (list com_raison_pose) materiau text Material (list com_materiau) revetement_interieur text Inner lining (list com_revetement_interieur) diametre_equivalent integer Nominal diameter longueur_terrain real Length measured on the ground sensible boolean If the pipe is sensitive

The drinking water pipes aep_canalisation also have the field fonction_canalisation (list aep_fonction_canalisation: adduction, transport, transport_distri, distribution), used by the network analysis algorithms.

docs.title: aep_vanne
docs.text: The valves of the drinking water network. Among their specific fields, the field etat_ouverture (list aep_etat_ouverture: ouverte, fermee, partiel_ouverte, partiel_fermee) is the opening state of the valve in normal operation. It is modified by the actions Fermer la vanne and Ouvrir la vanne, and used by the network analysis functions.

docs.title: Value lists
docs.text:
The schema stareau_valeur contains one table per value list of the geostandard, prefixed by aep_, ass_ or com_ (common to both networks), e.g. aep_type_vanne, ass_type_regard, com_materiau.

Field Type Description code text Code stored in the fields of the network tables. Unique. valeur text Label of the value description text Description of the value

The lists are filled when creating the database structure, from the CSV files of the geostandard. The following values are added to every list:

Code Label Description non_renseigne Non renseigné(e) Information being searched, or available but not entered non_concerne Non concerné(e) Information not possible or not relevant for the object non_valide Non validé(e) Information exists but is not officially validated non_determine Non déterminé(e) Information unknown or not available, and cannot be autre Autre Not in the list, see the comment

The list com_precision only gets the additional value N (Non renseigné(e)).

docs.title: Plugin tables
docs.text: The schema stareau contains the tables of the plugin.

docs.title: aep_vertex and aep_edge
docs.text:
The routing graph of the drinking water network, used by the pgRouting functions, and filled by the algorithm Fill AEP vertices and edges.

aep_vertex:

Field Type Description id integer Identifier of the vertex: the fid of the AEP network node, or an automatic identifier for a missing node fictif boolean True for a vertex created at the location of a missing node geom Point Geometry of the vertex

aep_edge:

Field Type Description id integer Identifier of the edge: the fid of the AEP pipe source integer Identifier of the vertex of the initial node target integer Identifier of the vertex of the terminal node cost real Cost from source to target: the length of the pipe reverse_cost real Cost from target to source: the length of the pipe geom LineString Geometry of the pipe

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
The version of the database structure, used by the plugin to know which upgrades must be run.

Field Type Description id integer Identifier me_version text Version of the database structure me_version_date date Date of the version me_status integer Status of the version: 1 for the active version

The tables test and glossary_test_category are examples, not used by the plugin.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
To use the plugin, you need to:

  • install QGIS Desktop
  • install the plugin for QGIS
  • add a connection to a PostgreSQL database with the PostGIS extension
  • install the database structure on this PostgreSQL database
  • create the QGIS administration project

docs.title: Get QGIS Desktop
docs.text:
The administrator must use the QGIS desktop software, version 3.34.x or above.

You can download QGIS in the official download page

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
At present, the plugin is not yet in QGIS official plugin repository, and it is experimental. To install the plugin, you need to:

  • open QGIS Plugin manager (menu Plugins),
  • in the Settings tab:
    • check the box Show also experimental plugins,
    • add a new repository with the URL https://github.com/3liz/qgis-stareau-plugin/releases/latest/download/plugins.xml,
  • in the All tab, search for the word StarEau and install the StarEau plugin.

After a successful installation, you should see a new dock called StarEau

For further details, you can have a look at 3liz documentation web page.

docs.title: Prepare the PostgreSQL database
docs.text:
The plugin stores all the data in a PostgreSQL database, with the PostGIS extension installed (to manage spatial data).

You need to have access to a PostgreSQL database, with enough rights to create schemas, tables and extensions. The installation creates the extensions postgis, uuid-ossp and hstore if they do not exist yet.

docs.title: pgRouting
docs.text:
The network analysis tools of the drinking water network need the pgRouting extension. It is not created by the plugin: a database administrator must install the pgRouting package on the server, then create the extension in the database:

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgrouting;

The functions use pgr_bdDijkstra, pgr_withPoints, pgr_trsp and pgr_findCloseEdges: use a recent version of pgRouting (3.4 or above). The plugin is tested with PostgreSQL 17 and pgRouting 4.

The other tools of the plugin work without pgRouting.

docs.title: Add a connection in QGIS
docs.text:
In QGIS, use the Datasource manager under the Layer menu to create a new PostgreSQL connection:

  • Activate the PostgreSQL tab (elephant icon)
  • Click on the New button
  • In the creation dialog, fill the needed information, and use the Test connection button to make sure the credentials are ok.

We advise to:

  • use a service connection instead of the basic authentication. See QGIS documentation
  • check the boxes Use estimated table metadata and Also list tables with no geometry

Once your connection is set up, you can create the database structure in your PostgreSQL database.

The algorithms below are available in the Processing toolbox, provider StarEau, and with the buttons of the group Install and configure of the StarEau panel.

docs.title: Configure the plugin
docs.text:
This algorithm will allow to configure the extension for the current QGIS project.

You must run this script before any other script.

Parameters:

  • PostgreSQL connection to the database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the current QGIS project. This connection will be used by default by the other algorithms.

The connection name is stored in the project variable stareau_connection_name: save the QGIS project to keep it.

docs.title: Create the database structure
docs.text:
Install the database structure with tables and functions on the chosen database connection.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the installation.
  • Overwrite the database schema and all data ?: if the schema already exists in the database, the algorithm stops with an error, unless this box is checked. In this case, the existing schemas are dropped with all their data and created again. Unchecked by default.
  • Schema name: prefix of the schemas to create. Default: stareau.
  • Geometry CRS: coordinate reference system of the geometries stored in the database. It must be a valid EPSG code. Default: EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93.

The algorithm creates the following schemas, prefixed by the chosen schema name:

Schema Content stareau Functions and triggers of the plugin, routing graph and metadata stareau_principale Parent tables: network nodes, pipes, common fields stareau_commun Tables shared by the AEP and ASS networks: rain gauges, piezometers, geolocation points stareau_aep Drinking water network stareau_aep_brcht Drinking water service connections stareau_ass Sanitation network stareau_ass_brcht Sanitation service connections stareau_defense_incendie Fire water points (PEI) stareau_valeur Value lists

Then it fills the value lists of the schema stareau_valeur, and stores the version of the database structure in the table stareau.metadata.

See Tables and fields for the description of the schemas and tables.

docs.title: Upgrade database structure
docs.text:
Upgrade the tables and functions in the chosen database.

If you have upgraded your QGIS plugin, you can run this script to upgrade your database to the new plugin version. The StarEau panel shows if an upgrade is needed, see Administration panel.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the upgrade.
  • Check this box to upgrade. No action will be done otherwise: safety checkbox. The algorithm refuses to run if it is not checked.
  • Schema name: prefix of the schemas to upgrade. Default: stareau.

The algorithm reads the version of the database structure in the table stareau.metadata, then runs the upgrade scripts of the newer versions, one by one. Nothing is done if the database is already up to date.

docs.title: Create your database local interface
docs.text:
This algorithm will create a new QGIS project file for administration purpose.

The generated QGIS project must then be opened by the administrator to create and edit the network data by using QGIS editing capabilities.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the new QGIS project.
  • Schema name: prefix of the schemas installed with the algorithm Create database structure. Default: stareau. The schema must exist in the database.
  • Geometry CRS: coordinate reference system of the QGIS project and its layers. Use the same CRS as the one chosen when creating the database structure. Default: EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93.
  • QGIS project file to create: choose the output file destination, with the extension .qgs. We advise you to choose a name reflecting the database name.

You can then open the generated QGIS project, see Administration project.

docs.title: User guide
docs.text:
The StarEau plugin stores the network data and most of the business logic inside a PostgreSQL database, following the StaR'Eau geostandard. The QGIS plugin helps to create and upgrade this database, to create a QGIS project to edit the data, to check the quality of the network and to analyse it.

This guide is split in four parts:

  • QGIS project and tools: the administration project, the panel of the plugin, and the actions available on the layers.
  • Processing algorithms: the algorithms provided by the plugin.
  • Network topology: how the database keeps the links between the pipes and the nodes when the data is edited.
  • Network analysis: the routing graph of the drinking water network and the tools based on pgRouting.

docs.title: Database model
docs.text:
All the data is stored inside a PostgreSQL database:

  • the tables of the StaR'Eau geostandard, split in several schemas: stareau_principale, stareau_aep, stareau_ass, stareau_valeur, etc.,
  • the schema stareau of the plugin, which contains:
    • trigger functions in charge of maintaining the network topology: links between the pipes and their initial and terminal nodes, precision of the coordinates,
    • functions to check the network: missing, orphan and duplicate nodes,
    • functions to walk the network: upstream and downstream of a sanitation node, paths and valves on the drinking water network with pgRouting,
    • the tables aep_vertex and aep_edge of the routing graph of the drinking water network,
    • the table metadata with the version of the database structure.

See Tables and fields for the description of the schemas and tables, Useful functions for the SQL functions, and the Database structure documentation for a complete description of the schema stareau.

docs.title: Administration tools
docs.text:
The plugin provides QGIS Processing algorithms which allow to:

  • create the database structure with all the schemas, tables, value lists, functions, etc.: Create database structure,
  • upgrade the structure automatically when upgrading the plugin: Upgrade database structure,
  • create a QGIS administration project with all the layers and actions: Create database local interface,
  • check the network: Get missing nodes, Get orphan nodes, Get duplicate nodes,
  • analyse the drinking water network: Fill AEP vertices and edges, Water intake points to nearest treatment, Treatments to nearest reservoir.

These algorithms, described in Processing algorithms, are available in the QGIS Processing toolbox and in the StarEau panel, which also shows the database connection used by the project and checks that the plugin and database versions match.

docs.title: Network analysis
docs.text:
The plugin uses the pgRouting extension to find paths on the drinking water network (AEP). See pgRouting to install the extension.

The sanitation network (ASS) is walked without pgRouting, by following the direction of the pipes: see the actions Upstream and Downstream.

docs.title: Routing graph
docs.text:
The pgRouting functions do not use the StaR'Eau tables directly, but a routing graph stored in two tables of the schema stareau:

Table Content aep_vertex The vertices: the AEP network nodes, with the same identifier as the node (id = fid of the node), and the missing nodes of the AEP network, with fictif = True aep_edge The edges: the AEP pipes, with the same identifier as the pipe (id = fid of the pipe), their source and target vertices, and their length as cost and reverse_cost

The water can flow in both directions in the graph: the direction of the pipes is not used.

The graph is built by the algorithm Fill AEP vertices and edges. It is not updated automatically: run this algorithm again after each modification of the drinking water network, otherwise the results of the analysis can be wrong, or an error can occur.

graph LR A[StaR'Eau tables<br>noeud_reseau, canalisation] -->|Fill AEP vertices and edges| B[Routing graph<br>aep_vertex, aep_edge] B --> C[Actions<br>Chercher traitement, reservoir, captage] B --> D[Algorithms<br>Water intake points to nearest treatment<br>Treatments to nearest reservoir] B --> E[SQL functions<br>aep_pgr_*]

docs.title: Path to the nearest target
docs.text:
From a node of the drinking water network, the function stareau.aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target returns the pipes of the shortest path to the nearest target:

  1. the 10 targets closest to the node (as the crow flies) are selected in the target table, e.g. aep_reservoir,
  2. the shortest paths to these targets are calculated on the graph (bidirectional Dijkstra),
  3. the shortest path is kept, and its pipes are returned.

The variant stareau.aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target_avoiding_closed_valves does the same, but the closed valves (etat_ouverture = 'fermee') cannot be crossed.

This calculation is used by:

  • the layer actions Chercher traitement, Chercher reservoir and Chercher captage, see Path to the nearest target,
  • the algorithms Water intake points to nearest treatment and Treatments to nearest reservoir, which run it for each water intake or for each treatment plant.

docs.title: Nearest valves
docs.text:
From a point located on a drinking water pipe, the function stareau.aep_pgr_nearest_vannes returns the valves to close to isolate this point: the first valves met in each direction when walking the network from the point. The valves are dead ends: the walk stops at the first valve.

The variant stareau.aep_pgr_nearest_closed_vannes only considers the closed valves: the open valves are crossed, and the walk stops at the first closed valves. It helps to find the closed valves which isolate a part of the network.

These functions are used by the action Nearest valves.

See Useful functions for the parameters of these functions.

docs.title: Processing algorithms
docs.text:
The plugin adds the provider StarEau to the QGIS Processing toolbox (menu Processing / Toolbox). All the algorithms are also available with the buttons of the StarEau panel.

Group Algorithm Usage Configuration Configure plugin Choose the PostgreSQL connection of the project Structure Create database structure Install the StaR'Eau schemas in the database Structure Upgrade database structure Upgrade the schemas after a plugin upgrade Administration Create database local interface Create the QGIS administration project Structure Get missing nodes Find the start and end points of the pipes without node Structure Get orphan nodes Find the nodes which are not linked to any pipe Structure Get duplicate nodes Find the orphan nodes located at the same place as another node Structure Fill AEP vertices and edges Build the routing graph of the drinking water network Structure Water intake points to nearest treatment Pipes between each water intake and the nearest treatment plant Structure Treatments to nearest reservoir Pipes between each treatment plant and the nearest reservoir

All the algorithms have a parameter Connection to the PostgreSQL database: by default, the connection chosen with the algorithm Configure plugin.

The algorithms are not available in the Processing model designer.

docs.title: Configure plugin
docs.text: Choose the PostgreSQL connection used by the current QGIS project. It must be run before the other algorithms. See Configure the plugin.

docs.title: Create database structure
docs.text: Install the StaR'Eau schemas, with their tables and value lists, and the schema stareau of the plugin, with its functions and triggers. See Create the database structure.

docs.title: Upgrade database structure
docs.text: Upgrade the database structure to the version of the plugin, after a plugin upgrade. The StarEau panel shows if an upgrade is needed. See Upgrade database structure.

docs.title: Create database local interface
docs.text: Create a QGIS administration project with all the layers and actions. See Create your database local interface and Administration project.

docs.title: Network checks
docs.text:
The three following algorithms help to find the topology errors of the network. They have the same parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database,
  • Schema name: the schema of the plugin. Default: stareau,
  • Network type: ASS (sanitation network) or AEP (drinking water network),
  • Destination: the output point layer.

The output layer is a copy of the result: run the algorithm again after correcting the data.

docs.title: Get missing nodes
docs.text:
Find the missing nodes: the start and end points of the pipes whose initial or terminal node is non_renseigne. Two pipes ending at the same point give only one missing node.

The output layer Missing nodes contains the fields:

Field Description fid Identifier of the missing node id_canalisation_upstream id_canalisation of the pipe ending at this point, if any id_canalisation_downstream id_canalisation of the pipe starting at this point, if any

To correct the errors, create a network node at the location of each missing node: the pipes are then linked automatically to the new node, see Network topology.

docs.title: Get orphan nodes
docs.text:
Find the orphan nodes: the network nodes which are neither the initial node nor the terminal node of any pipe.

The output layer Orphan nodes contains the fields of the table noeud_reseau. It can be a normal situation, for example for an isolated object, or an error, for example a node drawn more than 10 cm away from the end of a pipe.

docs.title: Get duplicate nodes
docs.text:
Find the duplicate nodes: the orphan nodes located at the same place as another network node.

The output layer Duplicate nodes contains the fields of the table noeud_reseau. These nodes can usually be deleted.

docs.title: Network analysis
docs.text: These algorithms work on the drinking water network, and need the pgRouting extension. See Network analysis.

docs.title: Fill AEP vertices and edges
docs.text:
Build the routing graph of the drinking water network, used by the pgRouting functions: the tables stareau.aep_vertex and stareau.aep_edge are emptied, then filled with:

  • the vertices: the AEP network nodes, and the missing nodes of the AEP network (fictif = True),
  • the edges: the AEP pipes, between their initial and terminal vertices. The cost of an edge is the length of the pipe, in both directions.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database,
  • Schema: the schema of the plugin. Default: stareau.

The graph is not updated automatically: run this algorithm again after each modification of the drinking water network, before using the network analysis tools.

docs.title: Water intake points to nearest treatment
docs.text:
For each water intake (aep_captage), find the path to the nearest treatment plant (aep_traitement) on the drinking water network, and create a layer with the pipes of these paths.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database,
  • Main schema: the schema of the plugin, e.g. stareau,
  • Pipes between water intake points and the nearest treatment: the output line layer.

The output layer Pipes layer contains the fields of the table aep_canalisation, and is styled by pipe function (fonction_canalisation): adduction, transport, transport-distribution, distribution. It helps to check the function of the pipes: the pipes carrying the raw water from the water intakes to the treatment plants should be adduction pipes.

docs.title: Treatments to nearest reservoir
docs.text:
For each treatment plant (aep_traitement), find the path to the nearest reservoir (aep_reservoir) on the drinking water network, and create a layer with the pipes of these paths.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database,
  • Main schema: the schema of the plugin, e.g. stareau,
  • Pipes between treatments and the nearest reservoir: the output line layer.

The output layer Pipes layer is styled by pipe function, like the previous algorithm.

docs.title: Administration project
docs.text:
The algorithm Create database local interface creates a QGIS administration project with the layers of all the tables of the database, and the actions needed to manage the network.

The project contains the following groups of layers:

  • AEP: the drinking water network, schemas stareau_aep and stareau_aep_brcht: pipes, service connections, water intakes, treatment plants, reservoirs, valves, pumping stations, etc.,
  • ASS: the sanitation network, schemas stareau_ass and stareau_ass_brcht: pipes, service connections, manholes, outlets, basins, pumping stations, collection points, etc.,
  • Commun: the shared objects of the schema stareau_commun: geolocation points, rain gauges, piezometers, and the fire water points pei,
  • Valeurs: the value lists of the schema stareau_valeur,
  • Bases: the parent tables of the schema stareau_principale:
    • noeud_reseau: all the network nodes, of all the networks,
    • canalisation: all the pipes, of all the networks,
    • emprise: the footprints.

The layers of the group Bases show the objects of all their child tables (see Table inheritance). To create a new object, use the layer of its specific table, for example aep_vanne for a valve or ass_canalisation for a sanitation pipe.

docs.title: Administration panel
docs.text:
The panel StarEau is used by the administrator to install and configure the database, and to run the tools of the plugin:

  • the group Information shows the PostgreSQL connection used by the project, the versions of the plugin and of the database structure, and checks that they match:
    • The database is OK: nothing to do,
    • The database version is older than your plugin version: run the algorithm Upgrade database structure,
    • The required schema version is older than the database structure version: upgrade the plugin,
  • the group Install and configure runs the algorithms Configure plugin (button Choose database connection), Create database structure, Create database local interface and Upgrade database structure,
  • the group Tools runs the algorithms which check and analyse the network: Get missing nodes, Get orphan nodes, Get duplicate nodes, Fill AEP vertices and edges, Treatments to nearest reservoir and Water intake points to nearest treatment,
  • the group Help opens this documentation.

The buttons are disabled, except Choose database connection, while the project has no valid database connection: run the algorithm Configure plugin first.

See Processing algorithms for the description of these algorithms.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text: The menu Help / Plugins / StarEau opens this documentation.

docs.title: Layer actions
docs.text:
Some layers of the administration project have actions, run by the StarEau plugin, which must be installed and activated:

Layers Action Usage canalisation, aep_canalisation, aep_canalisation_branchement, ass_canalisation, ass_canalisation_branchement Inverser la canalisation Reverse the direction of the pipe aep_vanne Fermer la vanne Close the valve aep_vanne Ouvrir la vanne Open the valve aep_captage, aep_vanne Chercher traitement Show the pipes to the nearest treatment plant aep_traitement, aep_reservoir, aep_vanne Chercher reservoir Show the pipes to the nearest reservoir aep_traitement, aep_vanne Chercher captage Show the pipes to the nearest water intake ASS node layers: ass_regard, ass_pompage, ass_bassin, ass_exutoire, ass_traitement, ass_pretraitement, ass_piece, ass_raccord, ass_point_collecte, ass_engouffrement_point, ass_ouvrage_special_point, ass_chambre_depollution Downstream Show the pipes downstream of the node same ASS node layers Upstream Show the pipes upstream of the node

To run an action on a feature, use the Identify Features tool and right-click on the feature in the map, or use the Run Feature Action tool of the Attributes toolbar.

The Python code of these actions is stored in the plugin: the actions of the project only call it, for example:

from qgis.utils import plugins

plugins['stareau'].run_action(
    'fermer_vanne',
    fid_vanne = [% fid %],
    id_layer = '[% @layer_id %]',
)

The same code can be used to add the actions to the layers of another QGIS project. The action must be of type Python. The layer must be a PostgreSQL layer of a StaR'Eau table: the actions check the geometry type and the fields of the layer, and display an error message in the QGIS message bar if the layer is not valid.

docs.title: Reverse a pipe
docs.text:
Action inverser_canalisation: reverses the direction of the line of the pipe.

Parameters: fid_canalisation (the fid of the pipe) and id_layer (a line layer).

The trigger functions of the database then update the initial and terminal nodes of the pipe, see Network topology. Use it when a pipe has been drawn in the wrong direction, for example against the flow direction of a sanitation network.

docs.title: Close or open a valve
docs.text:
Actions fermer_vanne and ouvrir_vanne: set the field etat_ouverture of the valve to fermee (closed) or ouverte (open).

Parameters: fid_vanne (the fid of the valve) and id_layer (a point layer with the field etat_ouverture).

The closed valves are used by the network analysis functions which avoid closed valves.

docs.title: Path to the nearest target
docs.text:
Action aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target: walks the drinking water network from the clicked node, and adds to the project a layer path_to_<target_table> with the pipes between the node and the nearest target: water intake, treatment plant or reservoir.

Parameters:

  • fid_noeud: the fid of the node,
  • id_layer: a point layer of a drinking water node table,
  • target_table: the table of the targets, starting with aep_, e.g. aep_traitement, aep_reservoir or aep_captage,
  • avoiding_closed_valves: False or True. If True, the closed valves cannot be crossed.
from qgis.utils import plugins

plugins['stareau'].run_action(
    'aep_pgr_path_to_nearest_target',
    fid_noeud = [% fid %],
    id_layer = '[% @layer_id %]',
    target_table = 'aep_reservoir',
    avoiding_closed_valves = False,
)

Note

All the parameters of an action must be given in the action code, even the ones with a default value in the Python function: otherwise the error Arguments invalides is displayed.

The message Aucun chemin n'a été trouvé pour atteindre la cible is displayed if no path is found.

This action needs pgRouting and an up to date routing graph: run the algorithm Fill AEP vertices and edges after editing the drinking water network. See Network analysis.

docs.title: Upstream and downstream of a sanitation node
docs.text:
Actions ass_downstream and ass_upstream: walk the sanitation network from the clicked node, following the direction of the pipes, and add to the project a layer Downstream or Upstream with all the pipes located downstream or upstream of the node.

Parameters: id_noeud (the id_noeud_reseau of the node) and id_layer (a point layer with the field id_noeud_reseau).

The walk stops at the pipes whose initial or terminal node is missing (non_renseigne). These actions do not need pgRouting.

docs.title: Nearest valves
docs.text:
Action aep_pgr_nearest_vannes: finds the valves to close to isolate a point of a drinking water pipe, and adds them to the project in a layer vannes_trouvées. This action is not configured in the administration project, but it can be added on a pipe layer, for example with the coordinates of the click on the map (action scope Canvas):

from qgis.utils import plugins

plugins['stareau'].run_action(
    'aep_pgr_nearest_vannes',
    id_layer = '[% @layer_id %]',
    point_x = [% @click_x %],
    point_y = [% @click_y %],
    closed_valves_only = False,
)

Parameters:

  • id_layer: a line layer of drinking water pipes,
  • point_x, point_y: the coordinates of the point, in EPSG:2154,
  • closed_valves_only: False or True. If True, only the closed valves are searched, and the open valves can be crossed.

See Nearest valves for the details of the calculation.

docs.title: Network topology
docs.text:
The links between the pipes and the network nodes are maintained by trigger functions of the schema stareau, each time a pipe or a node is created, moved or deleted. They work the same way in QGIS, in Lizmap or with SQL queries.

The triggers are installed on the parent tables stareau_principale.noeud_reseau and stareau_principale.canalisation and on each child table (PostgreSQL does not apply the triggers of a parent table to its child tables).

A pipe is only linked to a node of the same network family: a drinking water pipe (type_reseau = 'aep') to a drinking water node, a sanitation pipe (any other network type) to a sanitation node.

docs.title: Coordinates precision
docs.text:
The coordinates of the geometries of the nodes and of the pipes are rounded to 5 cm (ST_ReducePrecision(geom, 0.05)) when they are created or modified.

This trigger function, aa_before_geometry_insert_or_update_reduce_precision, is prefixed by aa_ to be run before the other triggers, which are run in alphabetical order.

docs.title: Create or move a pipe
docs.text:
When a pipe is created, or when its geometry is modified:

  • if a network node is located less than 10 cm from the start point of the line, the start point is moved on the node and the field noeudinitial gets the id_noeud_reseau of this node,
  • otherwise, noeudinitial gets the value non_renseigne,
  • the same rules apply to the end point of the line and the field noeudterminal.

If several nodes are closer than 10 cm, the closest one is used.

The direction of the line defines the initial and terminal nodes: use the action Inverser la canalisation to reverse a pipe drawn in the wrong direction. Its initial and terminal nodes are then swapped automatically.

docs.title: Create a node
docs.text:
When a network node is created, the pipes of the same network family:

  • whose noeudinitial is non_renseigne and whose start point is less than 10 cm from the node,
  • whose noeudterminal is non_renseigne and whose end point is less than 10 cm from the node,

are linked to the new node: their start or end point is moved on the node, and their field noeudinitial or noeudterminal gets the id_noeud_reseau of the node.

This allows to correct the missing nodes by creating the nodes after the pipes.

docs.title: Move a node
docs.text: When the geometry of a network node is modified, the start point of the pipes starting at this node and the end point of the pipes ending at this node are moved with the node.

docs.title: Delete a node
docs.text: When a network node is deleted, the fields noeudinitial and noeudterminal of the pipes linked to this node get the value non_renseigne. The geometries of the pipes are not modified.

docs.title: Disable the triggers
docs.text:
For a bulk import or a batch update, the trigger functions can be disabled for the current transaction or session with the setting stareau.graph.disable.trigger:

BEGIN;
-- Disable the StarEau triggers for this transaction
SET LOCAL stareau.graph.disable.trigger = '1';

-- Import or update the data here

COMMIT;

The precision of the coordinates and the links between the pipes and the nodes are then not computed: use the network checks algorithms afterwards.
